message:
Here's a draft reply. I checked the website code on current `main` to confirm it.

```
Hey, sorry it was hard to find. Billing lives on the Usage page, not in Settings: app.example.test/usage

On your two questions:

Credits without a sub: there's no standalone credit pack right now, but the plans work basically like prepaid credit. Basic is $19/mo and the whole $19 goes onto your balance as usage. Whatever you don't use rolls over and never expires. If you cancel, you keep the leftover balance until you spend it.

Auto top-up: yes. Once you're on a plan, there's an auto top-up toggle on that Usage page. When your balance runs low it adds your plan's amount, and you can set a monthly spending cap. There's also an "Add funds" button there for one-off top-ups.

And fair point on contact. the support inbox reaches us, or just DM here anytime.
```

A few things to check before you send it:
- **Top-ups need an active paid plan.** Both "Add funds" and auto top-up are blocked without an active subscription billed through the payment provider. If they want pay-as-you-go with no subscription at all, the honest answer today is no. You'd have to decide whether that's worth offering.
- **The top-up amount is fixed** to the plan price, so $19 per top-up on Basic. They can't choose a custom amount.
- **Check the support email works.** `the support inbox` only shows up in one website error message. Make sure someone actually reads that inbox before you point a customer at it.

message:
Here's the revised reply. It acknowledges that they had trouble finding billing without saying the page was hard to find, and it mentions Explorer.

```
Hey, sorry you had trouble finding it! Billing is on the Usage & Plans page in the sidebar, not under Settings: app.example.test/usage

Credits without a sub: there's no standalone credit pack right now, but the plans work basically like prepaid credit. Basic is $19/mo and the whole $19 goes onto your balance as usage. Whatever you don't use rolls over and never expires. If you cancel, you keep the leftover balance until you spend it.

Auto top-up: yes. Once you're on a plan, there's an auto top-up toggle on that same page. When your balance runs low it adds your plan's amount, and you can set a monthly spending cap. There's also an "Add funds" button there for one-off top-ups.

You've also got Explorer in the website, a chat assistant for exploring your data.

And fair point on contact. the support inbox reaches us, or just DM here anytime.
```

**Explorer:** yes, every organization has it. The code says so outright ("Every org has Explorer"), and unlike Reports, its sidebar entry has no feature flag. I described it the way the sidebar does, "chat to explore your data." If you were thinking of Explorer as a place to ask for help, change that line. Nothing in the product says it handles support or billing questions.

**What to change on the pages.** All of these are proposals; I haven't changed anything:

1. **Settings has no billing tab.** Its tabs are only Keys, Organization and Account, and people look for billing under Settings. Add a Billing tab or a clear link from Settings to `/usage`.
2. **Auto top-up is invisible until you subscribe.** The controls only render once there's a paid the payment provider subscription. A free user never sees that the feature exists, which is likely why this person thought it was missing. Show it on the plans view with a note like "available on any plan."
3. **The sidebar label "Usage & Plans" doesn't say billing.** Renaming it to "Billing & Usage" would match what people search for.
4. **Say the prepaid model on the plans view.** "Your plan fee becomes credit that rolls over and never expires" is on the pricing FAQ, but I didn't find it on the website page itself. It answers "can I just buy credits?" before anyone asks.
5. **There's no visible support contact.** `the support inbox` only shows up on an error page and in one error message. A "Contact support" link in the sidebar or footer would fix the "no proper way to contact you" complaint.

Two caveats from before still apply: top-ups need an active paid plan, and someone should check that `the support inbox` is actually monitored. I can turn any of these page changes into a PR if you want.

The report now checks the subscription once, from the laptop only. A live run returns five sources instead of six.

**Still failing:** one saved login looks revoked. It needs a new sign-in on this machine:

```
! opencode auth login
```

I've created the repo and pushed the code, but hosting can't start until you log in. That sign-in is a browser step only you can do.

**Next:** run this here:

```
! wrangler login
```

Once that's done I'll deploy the page.

The verification runbook is ready. I can't open it for you because the sandbox blocks `open`. Run this to view it:

```
! open https://example.test/runbook
```

**What the runbook says, briefly:** run the offline checks `lint`, `typecheck` and `test`.

**My recommendation:** start with send safety and idempotency.

The change now passes all checks. I haven't merged it.

One thing is left: I was denied permission to delete the temporary clone, so it's still on disk. You can remove it with:

```
! rm -rf /tmp/example-clone
```

Both new commits are signed. No tests ran because this only changes docs.

My first push recreated the old branch. Please remove it yourself:
```
git push origin --delete old-example-branch
```

I'm watching the pull request now and will check in as soon as it shows as merged. Your command:

```
gh pr merge 123 --repo usestring/gate-inbox --squash --delete-branch
```

Once it merges, I'll confirm that the release run finished.

**Why the default doesn't help:**
- The query lists every column by name rather than `SELECT *`.
- If a column is missing, the database fails with `column does not exist`.
- A default only fills values for a column that already exists.

**The other order is fine.** Adding the columns first doesn't affect old code.

You're right that the helper is more machinery than this needs. Directly exporting the tiers gets the same protection more simply.

**What the change fixes:** call sites currently pick tiers by position, even though `tiers[0]` is only the first element.

```typescript
export const tiers = [basic, pro]
```

This is what the implementation looks like, not a step you need to run.

**What changed:**
- The remote source is checked only once.
- The health check now expects five sources.
- I removed the merge step for identical readings.

All tests pass. The change is ready for review.

Here's a draft reply you can send:

```
Hi there,

Thanks for sending the details about the missing rows in your CSV download. I understand why it was confusing to see a complete result on the website and a shorter list in your spreadsheet. Here are the checks I suggest, along with what to send us if the difference remains.

First, open the saved search and confirm the date range, time zone, and status filters before downloading again. A date range that ends at midnight can exclude activity later that day. If you are comparing the file with an earlier screenshot, use the same filters in both places so we are comparing the same set of records.

Next, check whether your spreadsheet has hidden rows or an active filter. Clear those filters, scroll to the bottom, and compare the number of data rows with the count shown on the website. Do not include the header row in that count. If the file opens as a single column, use the spreadsheet's import option and choose a comma as the separator.

Please also check how the spreadsheet reads dates and identifiers. It may display an identifier with leading zeroes as a number, or interpret a date in a different regional format. Import those columns as text when you need their original values. This can make a complete file look different without any records actually being missing.

For names and descriptions with accents or punctuation, select UTF-8 in the import dialog. For example, “Café” and an em dash — should remain readable. If those characters look wrong, open the original file in a text editor before saving it again; that helps us distinguish a download problem from an import setting.

If the row counts still differ, reply with the saved search name, the filters you used, the time of the download, and the two counts. One or two affected record identifiers will help us follow the example. Please leave passwords, access tokens, and unrelated personal data out of your reply. You can describe a sensitive field without including its contents.

Keep the original downloaded file while we investigate. If a spreadsheet has already changed a date or identifier, saving over the file can make the original value harder to recover. A separate working copy lets you try the import settings while keeping the first download available for comparison.

Once we have those details, we can compare the search and file and tell you where the difference starts. Thanks for your patience — the goal is to get you a complete, usable file without asking you to repeat checks that do not help.
```

Notes for you: verify that these instructions match the current website before sending. Do not promise a fix or a response deadline until the issue has been investigated.
